blocks.title: 1. The Core Concept: Buy Low, Sell High
blocks.content: Every business operates on one simple principle: buy something at a low price (Cost Price) and sell it at a higher price (Selling Price). The difference is your **Profit**. If you sell for LESS than you paid, you make a **Loss**. Understanding profit and loss percentages is essential for business, shopping, and economics.

blocks.title: 2. The Rules: The Formulas
blocks.content:
• **Profit** = Selling Price (SP) - Cost Price (CP).
• **Loss** = CP - SP.
• **Profit %** = (Profit / CP) x 100.
• **Loss %** = (Loss / CP) x 100.
• Critical: percentage is ALWAYS calculated on the **Cost Price**, not the selling price!
• **Discount %** = (Discount / Marked Price) x 100.

blocks.title: 3. Step-by-Step: Finding the Cost Price
blocks.content:
If you know the selling price and profit percentage:

1. SP = CP + Profit.
2. SP = CP + (Profit% / 100) x CP.
3. SP = CP x (1 + Profit%/100).
4. So CP = SP / (1 + Profit%/100).

For loss: CP = SP / (1 - Loss%/100).

blocks.title: 4. Worked Example: Finding Profit %
blocks.content:
A shopkeeper buys a toy for Rs. 200 and sells it for Rs. 250.

**Step 1:** Profit = SP - CP = 250 - 200 = Rs. 50.
**Step 2:** Profit % = (50/200) x 100 = 25%.

**Final Answer: The profit percentage is 25%.**

blocks.title: 5. Common Pitfalls
blocks.content: The deadliest mistake: calculating profit/loss percentage on the SELLING PRICE instead of the COST PRICE. If CP = 200 and SP = 250, Profit% = (50/200) x 100 = 25%. But if you mistakenly use SP: (50/250) x 100 = 20%. That's the wrong answer! Profit and loss percentages are ALWAYS based on Cost Price.
